text: No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The best way of avenging thyself is not to become like the wrong-doer.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: If it is not right, do not do it: if it is not true, do not say it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Very little indeed is necessary for living a happy life.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Loss is nothing else than change.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The universe is transformation: life is opinion.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Such as are thy habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of thy mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if thou wilt ever dig.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Take away thy opinion, and then there is taken away the complaint, "I have been harmed." Take away the complaint, "I have been harmed," and the harm is taken away.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Be like the promontory against which the waves continually break, but it stands firm and tames the fury of the water around it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Confine thyself to the present.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: If any man is able to convince me and show me that I do not think or act right, I will gladly change; for I seek the truth, by which no man was ever injured.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: How ridiculous and what a stranger he is who is surprised at anything which happens in life.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Men exist for the sake of one another.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The art of life is more like the wrestler's art than the dancer's, in respect of this, that it should stand ready and firm to meet onsets which are sudden and unexpected.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: How much trouble he avoids who does not look to see what his neighbor says or does or thinks, but only to what he does himself, that it may be just and pure.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Thou wilt give thyself relief if thou doest every act of thy life as if it were the last.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Everything harmonizes with me, which is harmonious to thee, O Universe.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Begin the morning by saying to thyself, I shall meet with the busybody, the ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious, unsocial.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Of things some are in our power, and others are not.
author: Epictetus

text: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
author: Epictetus

text: Seek not that the things which happen should happen as you wish; but wish the things which happen to be as they are, and you will have a tranquil flow of life.
author: Epictetus

text: If you would improve, submit to be considered without sense and foolish with respect to externals.
author: Epictetus

text: Never say about anything, I have lost it, but say I have restored it.
author: Epictetus

text: It is circumstances (difficulties) which show what men are.
author: Epictetus

text: Every habit and faculty is maintained and increased by the corresponding actions.
author: Epictetus

text: Remember that it is not he who reviles you or strikes you, who insults you, but it is your opinion about these things as being insulting.
author: Epictetus

text: You may fetter my leg, but my will not even Zeus himself can overpower.
author: Epictetus

text: Nothing great, said Epictetus, is produced suddenly, since not even the grape or the fig is.
author: Epictetus

text: Do not admire your clothes, and then you will not be angry with the thief.
author: Epictetus

text: We ought to exercise ourselves in small things, and beginning with them to proceed to the greater.
author: Epictetus

text: It is a man's own opinions which disturb him.
author: Epictetus

text: The origin of perturbation is this, to wish for something, and that this should not happen.
author: Epictetus

text: Keep by every means what is your own; do not desire what belongs to others.
author: Epictetus

text: To be instructed is this, to learn to wish that everything may happen as it does.
author: Epictetus

text: The condition and characteristic of an uninstructed person is this: he never expects from himself profit (advantage) nor harm, but from externals.
author: Epictetus

text: Nothing, Lucilius, is ours, except time.
author: Seneca

text: Hold every hour in your grasp.
author: Seneca

text: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
author: Seneca

text: What man can you show me who places any value on his time, who reckons the worth of each day, who understands that he is dying daily?
author: Seneca

text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
author: Seneca

text: Everywhere means nowhere.
author: Seneca

text: Men learn while they teach.
author: Seneca

text: If you would be loved, love.
author: Hecato, quoted by Seneca

text: There are more things, Lucilius, likely to frighten us than there are to crush us; we suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca

text: Nature's wants are slight; the demands of opinion are boundless.
author: Seneca

text: Real joy, believe me, is a stern matter.
author: Seneca

text: You need a change of soul rather than a change of climate.
author: Seneca

text: When a man does not know what harbour he is making for, no wind is the right wind.
author: Seneca

text: He suffers more than is necessary, who suffers before it is necessary.
author: Seneca

text: Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
author: Seneca

text: The greatest flaw in life is that it is always imperfect, and that a certain part of it is postponed.
author: Seneca

text: Aye, the willing soul Fate leads, but the unwilling drags along.
author: Cleanthes, translated by Seneca
